description: Expected NLP results for the nine OCR sample files in ocr_samples/ (roadmap Steps 37 and 40). Labels were read from the original screenshots and approved by Prakriti. A null means the parser must leave that field empty. OCR damage is NOT corrected here: where the OCR lost or scrambled a date, the date must stay empty.

payment_notice.json.note: Last date for payment is 4 November 2026. The OCR wrote 'Nert'; the title uses 'next' from 'your next semester' in the same text.

screenshot 2.json.note: The image says 11 January, 7 PM. The OCR lost the '11', so no date can be read and event_datetime stays empty. The 7 PM is kept in date_time_expression because the contract keeps an event's time there when the date is unknown.

screenshot 3.json.note: Two separate dates (27 and 30 October 2026), so no single date is chosen; both are kept in the description. The OCR moved '6th' away from the title.

screenshot 4.json.note: Debate on 9 October 2026 at 3:30 PM (a date before the reference date is still an event).

screenshot 5.json.note: Webinar on 5 June, 4:30-5:30 PM IST. The OCR separated 'June' from '05', so the date is not reliable and stays empty.

screenshot 6.json.note: Informational notice with no instruction. 'Meeting held on ...' is a past mention, not an event.

screenshot 7.json.note: The image says last date 9 Sep 2026, but the OCR scattered '9th', '2026' and 'Sep'. The date cannot be read reliably, so it stays empty.

screenshot 8.json.note: Viva on 4th and 5th April 2019, reporting from 09.00 a.m. The start date is used and the range is kept in the description. A past date is still an event.

screenshot 9.json.note: Invited talk on 9 October at 8:00 PM (no year on the poster; the nearest year is used). The OCR wrote 'lot' for 'IoT'; that is not corrected because the text gives nothing to correct it from.
